the_question: can a specification read off a module's OWN STRUCTURE judge a real change, when no test was written and no intent was stated?
the_result: 0 of 40 real commits, and 0 of the 19 that ship no test, were rejected by any law derived from the new code's own structure. The laws were not vacuous in the arithmetic sense -- 188 were confirmed -- but 174 of them are bare TOTALITY and 14 are IDEMPOTENCE: structure can barely STATE a law about real library code, and where it can, the real change does not violate it.

what_a_kill_is: EFFECT CERTIFICATION, NEVER INTENT VERIFICATION. A law confirmed on the fixed code rejects the parent because the change altered structure-implied behaviour. It does not say the change is what anyone asked for; a wrong change would be confirmed and its parent rejected all the same.
